units.summary: ParseQuantity now calls CacheString on the two result paths that previously left the cached string empty (int64 fast path and inf.Dec path). Parsed quantities now always carry q.s, which affects reflect.DeepEqual comparisons and avoids recomputation at encode time.
units.headline: ParseQuantity now always caches the canonical string
units.reason: Changes the internal state of every parsed Quantity, which is visible to DeepEqual comparisons and the encoding paths.
risk_signals: internal state of widely used type changed
focus: callers or tests comparing parsed Quantity with reflect.DeepEqual against hand-built values
extra allocation and canonicalization cost on every parse

units.summary: String no longer writes the computed string back to the receiver, which removes a data race when String is called concurrently on a shared Quantity. Quantities built without ParseQuantity now recompute the string on every call.
units.headline: Quantity.String no longer mutates the receiver
units.reason: Removes a side effect that callers and tests may have relied on, and changes performance and concurrency characteristics of a hot path.
focus: code that relied on String() populating q.s, such as DeepEqual comparisons
repeated recomputation for quantities not built by ParseQuantity, for example in JSON and proto encoding

units.summary: Adds a public CacheString method that computes the canonical string and stores it on the receiver. It is meant for callers that own the instance, and always writes so that races are detectable.
units.headline: New public Quantity.CacheString method caches canonical string
units.reason: Adds a public API on a core type that mutates the receiver.
focus: that callers cannot invoke it on shared instances
that cached s is cleared by every mutating operation so it cannot go stale

units.summary: The test now expects ParseQuantity to set the cached string, replacing the earlier assertions that it was empty after parse and set after String. The expectation was changed to match the new behavior.
units.headline: TestQuantityString expectations flipped to match cached-on-parse behavior
units.reason: An assertion was inverted to match new behavior and another was removed, which could hide regressions.
risk_signals: expectations changed to match new behavior
focus: that the removed check that String populates q.s is intentionally dropped

units.summary: New test covers CacheString on a quantity with no cached string, a repeat call, and a nil receiver. Test-only, no production impact.
units.headline: Add test for Quantity.CacheString

units.summary: The benchmark is rewritten as per-case sub-benchmarks using b.Loop, and the separate Precalc benchmark is removed. Benchmarks only, no production impact.
units.headline: Rewrite string benchmark as sub-benchmarks, drop Precalc variant

units.summary: The BinarySI string benchmark is converted to per-case sub-benchmarks with b.Loop. Benchmark-only.
units.headline: BinarySI string benchmark converted to sub-benchmarks

units.summary: The parse benchmark now iterates the shared test case inputs as sub-benchmarks and no longer checks the error. Benchmark-only.
units.headline: Parse benchmark now runs over shared test case inputs
